Newlines inside the JS source string need to be actual "\n" escapes. With single-quoted shell, \\n stays as \\n? No—shell single quotes preserve backslashes literally, so \\n stays \\n (two chars backslash backslash? no). In single quotes, `\n` is backslash + n, passed as-is to node. In JS inside a double-quoted string, "\n" is newline. Good. But I need the written file to contain `'\n'` sequence, i.e., backslash-n in the JS source.
